newsitem.title: BULGARIA: INSTANT VIEW - Bulgaria pegging lev to mark.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bulgaria pegging lev to mark.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on Bulgaria's interim cabinet proposal to peg the lev to the mark as anchor currency in a fixed exchange rate regime due to be introduced in July.

DAVID BOREN, VICE PRESIDENT EMERGING MARKETS RESEARCH, SALOMON BROTHERS - The advantage of the mark over the dollar suggests that the exchange rate would be linked closer to Bulgaria's trade flows as trade with Europe grows. This should also mean that the currency board will be sustainable over a longer period.

KRASSEN STANCHEV, DIRECTOR, INSTITUTE FOR MARKET ECONOMICS - I would prefer the dollar as an anchor currency as the majority of the population are familiar with and have more confidence in the dollar rather than the mark. The psychological effect of this proposal sought by the stabilisation council is to prompt people to convert their savings into marks and thus return their matress money to the banks.

GALINA DIMITROVA, ECONOMIST, BULGARIAN INVESTMENT BANK - I share the opinion that the mark will ease Bulgaria's integration in the European monetary system in the future despite the current prevalence of dollar transactions. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
